$comment: Plate prompts for the homepage card alternatives (the grounded, pedestal-free directions of 'The Three'). 12 entries = 4 concepts x 3 fragrances. `prompt` is the product-free plate prompt for FLUX / Kling / any prose generator; `midjourney` is the same scene as a Midjourney v6 string with its parameters and `--no`; `negative` is for tools that have a negative field (FLUX and Kling have none: the plate prompts avoid product words instead). The approved flacon is composited on top, never generated. Checked by `pnpm home:images check`.

frame.layout: The tile is aspect-ratio 4/5 (.rh-tile__media). Keep the lower-right 12% and the vertical centre of the right edge quiet: the chevron and the two dots sit there.
frame.placement: Contact line at y about 80% of the frame height; the flacon about 62-64% of the frame height (the old cards shrank it to about 45%).

flaconSpec.rule: The bottle always stands directly on the ground surface: no pedestal, stand, stool, block or plinth anywhere in any plate.
flaconSpec.approved: 50 ml thick-base flint glass flacon with clean vertical lines, heavy matte black cylindrical cap, centred off-white cotton-rag label reading THE RARESKIN / fragrance name / ESSENTIALS | 50ml, crystal-clear liquid.
flaconSpec.briefLabel: EXTRAIT DE PARFUM · 50 ML / 1.7 FL. OZ. is NOT adopted: the approved mockups and the product pages carry ESSENTIALS | 50ml (decision of 2026-11-06). Changing the label means new approved bottle art for all three products.
flaconSpec.briefLiquid: Amber / golden-amber liquid (brief, concept 4) is NOT adopted: the approved liquid is crystal clear. Concept 4's gold comes from the sun, not the extrait.
flaconSpec.neverGenerate: Never let a generator draw the bottle or its label: label text always comes out garbled. For a mood-only exploration add this clause to a prose prompt, and discard the text it draws: 'a 50 ml flint-glass perfume flacon with a thick clear base and clean straight sides, a heavy matte black cylindrical cap, an off-white cotton paper label'.

workflow: 1. Generate the plate (Kling kling-image-v3_0_omni text_to_image at 3:4, about 2 credits; or Midjourney / FLUX at 4:5) and reject any plate that contains a pedestal, a bottle, text or an extra prop.
2. Crop to 4:5 above any generator logo (Kling returns 1760x2368 for 3:4).
3. Composite the approved flacon with design-explorations/packaging-renders/homepage/place_bottles.py (see each entry's `composite`).
5. In public/images/assets-manifest.json set status to final, fix the alt, re-measure overlayTone (chevron colour), and bump assetVersion.

concepts.label: Grounded stone
concepts.direction: Concept 1 - Grounded Seamless Surface (Direct Earth & Stone): the flacon stands directly on honed limestone, raw oak or basalt with its ingredients lying beside the base.

concepts.label: Studio light
concepts.direction: Concept 2 - Architectural Chiaroscuro & Studio Bleed: the flacon on an off-white plaster sweep, window-frame shadows across the backdrop, merging with the page.

concepts.label: Mineral bed
concepts.direction: Concept 3 - Raw Mineral & Botanical Bed: low-angle macro, the base slightly embedded in marble dust, crushed spice or volcanic sand.

concepts.label: Liquid light
concepts.direction: Concept 4 - Optical Caustics & Liquid Refraction: the flacon on a shallow water film or an optical-glass plate, warm sun throwing golden caustics beside it.

prompts.prompt: Quiet editorial still life, portrait 4:5 frame. A wide pale honed limestone tabletop with fine veining fills the lower half of the frame, runs to the bottom edge of the frame and meets a softly textured lime-washed plaster wall in warm off-white a little more than halfway down the frame. Soft early-morning window light at about 5200 K enters from the upper left and lays one gentle diagonal sun bar across the wall; shadows are soft-edged. On the limestone, level with the middle of the tabletop and not at the back, lie exactly one freshly sliced bergamot half, pebbled yellow-green rind with the pale pith segments facing the camera, at the very left edge of the frame, partly cut by the frame edge, and a small scatter of five white jasmine petals at the very right edge of the frame, partly cut by the frame edge. Between them the whole middle of the tabletop is wide, empty, bare limestone with nothing on it. Camera at tabletop height, tilted down about 12 degrees, 100 mm macro lens at f/5.6, shallow depth of field on the wall, fine natural film grain. Calm, airy palette of ivory, pale stone and soft lime green.

prompts.prompt: Moody editorial still life, portrait 4:5 frame. A wide honed black volcanic basalt floor with a fine matte grain and a few tiny pores fills the entire lower half of the frame from the left edge to the right edge; it is one continuous flat surface with no borders, no frame, no cracks and no edges, and it meets a charcoal-grey plaster wall, which falls to near black at the top, a little more than halfway down the frame. Low camera at surface height, tilted down only about 10 degrees, so the floor is seen at a shallow grazing angle. A soft cool light at about 5600 K from the upper left rims the grain; a faint warm 3000 K edge light comes from the right. A single thin wisp of white smoke rises against the dark wall only, above the line where the wall meets the floor, at about three quarters of the frame width, curls once and thins to nothing by the upper third of the frame; the smoke never crosses the floor. In the lower left corner of the frame only a small corner of a dark brown stitched leather strip is visible, cut by the left and bottom frame edges, and in the lower right corner about a dozen black peppercorns are scattered on the floor, partly cut by the right and bottom frame edges. The whole middle of the floor, from the foreground to the wall, is wide, empty, bare basalt with nothing on it. 100 mm macro lens at f/4, fine natural film grain. Palette of charcoal, graphite, warm brown and a single thread of white.

prompts.prompt: Fine-art product photography background with nothing in the middle, portrait 4:5 frame, shot perfectly level and straight-on, the camera at the height of the water, the line where the wall meets the water exactly horizontal and a little more than halfway down the frame. A very shallow, perfectly still sheet of clear water, a few millimetres deep, lies over a flat pale honed travertine floor that fills the whole lower half of the frame from the left edge to the right edge, with no borders, no edges, no tray and no waves, and runs to the bottom edge of the frame. The wall is a soft pale plaster, mirrored faintly in the water. Warm low sun at about 3800 K from the upper left sets a golden-white net of caustic light shimmering on the stone beneath the water in the right half of the frame, with a faint echo near the left edge. At the very left edge of the frame, partly cut by it, one white jasmine flower rests on the stone, and at the very right edge, partly cut by it, one thin curl of bergamot zest rests on the stone. The whole middle of the floor, from the foreground to the wall, is a calm, empty, evenly lit stretch of still water with nothing on it. No people, no faces, no hands. 100 mm lens at f/5.6, fine natural film grain. Pale ivory, soft gold and a touch of lime green.
